fields.h1: Build a Pre-Order Form That Stops at What You Can Make

fields.features_heading: What a Pre-Order Run Needs From Its Form
fields.features_subheading: A pre-order form takes orders for items you have not made or shipped yet. It has to know your limits and your dates.
fields.feature_1:
A ready date beside every item

Each item on the form shows the date it ships or is ready for pickup, beside the quantity box. Change a date by prompting, and every confirmation sent after that carries it.
fields.feature_2:
Limits set by what you can make

Give each item the most you can make, such as one kiln load or a single batch. The form counts orders as they come in and closes the item when the last unit is taken.
fields.feature_3:
A cutoff date that closes the form

Pick the last day you take orders. Once it passes, the form swaps the order button for a closed notice with your next date, and nothing new lands in the queue after it.
fields.feature_4:
A production count from every order

Every pre-order is saved to a database you own. A dashboard totals units by item and by ready date, and the morning bake list or the week's build list fits on one screen.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders before pickup day

The app emails each buyer a set number of days before pickup with the items and the total. You get an email or Slack alert when an item sells out or a large order arrives.
fields.feature_6:
Your code on GitHub

Export the full code behind the form, with its order rules and database, to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can then read every line and change it there.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Pre-Order Runs, One Rule Each
fields.tab_content_1:
40 pies an hour, and 10 am is gone

Ambrine Bakehouse bakes pies to order for Wed, Nov 25, the day before Thanksgiving, and each pickup hour holds 40 pies. Once the 10 am hour has 40, the form stops offering it. Zubair Lockett orders 2 pumpkin pies at $28 each, $56 in all. He takes the 2 pm hour.
fields.tab_content_2:
Knife 301 is spot 1 on the waitlist

Tavish Forge hammers out one run of 300 chef's knives at $145 each, and the form says the run ships the week of Jan 11. Every order after 300 goes to the waitlist for the next run. Winnifred Mabe places order 301 and becomes spot 1.
fields.tab_content_3:
Order by Feb 16 for an inscription

Petronella Arkwright signs every pre-ordered copy of her new novel, which releases on Tue, Mar 2. She closes inscriptions on Feb 16, which leaves 14 days for signing. Cosmin Ostby pre-orders on Feb 19. The form hides the inscription box and saves his order as a signed copy with no inscription.
fields.tab_content_4:
Two days ahead, her order arrives by email

Kestrel Hollow Nursery grows its spring starts to order, closes pre-orders on Mar 15, and holds pickup on Sat, Apr 24. Isidora Quarles ordered 6 tomato starts and 2 pepper starts at $4.50 each, $36 in all. On Thu, Apr 22, the app emails her that list and her total, 2 days before pickup.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Pre-Order Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set your limits and dates, then create a pre-order form that applies them with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the items and what you can make
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the date each item is ready
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose the fields an order needs
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the limits and the cutoff date
fields.howto_step_1_des: List each item you will take pre-orders for with its price and the most you can make or source before it is due. Base the number on what you produced in a recent week, not on what you hope to sell.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Set the date each item ships, or the day buyers can collect it, and show it beside the item on the form. Choose a date you can meet at the limit from step 1, with a day spare for packing.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the buyer's name and email, then the quantity of each item and any option that changes it, such as a flavor or an inscription. Add a shipping address only if you ship, and a pickup slot only if buyers collect.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give each item or pickup slot its limit, and choose the last day the form takes orders. Decide what a buyer sees once an item sells out: a closed notice, or a numbered waitlist for the next batch.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the form in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt to Emergent that carries your notes from the first four steps. Emergent builds the form with the database behind it, and you change a limit or a date later by prompting, without starting over.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Ask for an email to each buyer before pickup and a Slack alert to you when an item sells out. If orders also belong in your store or another tool, connect it through its API so the two stay in sync.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Place test orders that fill one item to its limit, arrive after the cutoff, and join the waitlist. Check each result, then publish the form on its own link or on your custom domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits.

faq_plan.q: What is a pre order form?
faq_plan.a: A pre order form takes orders for an item before it is made or in stock. It records who ordered what, and when each order will be ready. The seller then makes or buys stock against those totals.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a pre-order form?
faq_plan.ref: How do I create a pre-order form?

prov.original: How do I create a pre-order form?

faq_plan.a: List your items, the most you can make of each, and the date each one is ready. Describe that in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, and it returns a working form that stops taking orders for an item at its limit and closes on your cutoff date.

faq_plan.q: What should a pre order form template include?
faq_plan.a: A pre order form template should include the buyer's contact details, each item with its price and a quantity box, the ready or ship date, and pickup or shipping details. Add a limit per item and a closing date. If you also keep a pre order form PDF at the counter for walk-in buyers, enter those orders into the same list to keep the counts right.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a free pre order form for a small business?
faq_plan.a: To make a free pre order form, start on Emergent's free tier. The free tier covers building and publishing. Describe your items, prices, limits, and ready dates in one prompt. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, and a busy launch week never closes the form early. A school or team collecting sizes before a season can build a uniform order form the same way.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a pre-order form stop taking orders when an item sells out?
faq_plan.a: Set a limit on each item, and the form closes that item once submitted orders reach it. Count units, not orders: a buyer who takes 3 uses 3 of the limit. Then choose what a late buyer sees, such as a sold-out label, a date for the next batch, or a waitlist.

faq_plan.q: What should I do when orders from a pre-order form cannot ship on the promised date?
faq_plan.a: Tell each buyer before the date passes and ask whether they will wait. For most goods a customer orders by mail, telephone, fax, or on the Internet, the FTC's mail order rule says a seller who can ship later must seek the customer's consent to the delay. A seller who cannot ship must promptly cancel the order and make a full refund.

faq_plan.q: How do I turn pre-order form orders into a production plan?
faq_plan.a: Add up what each item needs for each ready date, then work back from the earliest date to set what gets made each day. Every order sits in a database you own, and a dashboard on that table shows the daily list. Some pre-orders end in a visit, such as installing shelving a buyer ordered; schedule that visit on a work order form.

faq_plan.q: How do customers choose a pickup time on a pre-order form?
faq_plan.a: Buyers pick from a list of pickup slots, each with its own limit, and a full slot drops off the list. Size each slot by how many orders your counter can hand out in that time. Repeat the slot and the pickup address in the confirmation email.

faq_plan.q: When should a pre-order form close?
faq_plan.a: Close it early enough to buy supplies and make everything before the ready date. Work back from that date: production time, plus the lead time on supplies, plus a day of slack. Set two closing rules on pre order forms with a fixed run, the date and the limit, and stop at whichever comes first.

faq_plan.q: Can one pre-order form handle sizes and colors?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each item a size and a color choice, and set the limit per variant when each one runs out on its own, such as 40 mediums and 20 larges. In a form built with Emergent, you add a size or a color later by prompting. For shirts ordered in a size grid, a t shirt order form with a quantity per size is a closer fit.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, Typeform, forms.app, AidaForm, Formaloo), two Pinterest boards of printable sheets and an Adobe guide to building an order form in a PDF. Every one stops at a list of fields. None handles what makes a pre-order different from an order: the item does not exist yet, so the form has to cap what you can make, close on a date, say when the item ships or is ready, and keep the buyer informed until pickup. This page shows four sellers running one pre-order rule each (a pickup-hour cap, a limited run with a waitlist, a personalization cutoff before release day, a pickup reminder), and the FAQ covers the late-shipment duty with the FTC rule quoted with its scope.
